Data Storage & External Services

The catalog is stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6 when mock data is disabled; otherwise a process-local mock catalog is used. Product images can use Azure Blob Storage, while Azure AD, managed-identity SQL authentication, and Application Insights instrumentation are configuration-dependent. Redis session support is present only as a commented configuration example.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or SQL-backed catalog services and mock or Azure-backed image services from application settings.
  • The application uses a single web deployment with server-rendered pages, in-process service calls, and no message broker or API gateway.
  • SQL Server access supports either a configured connection string or an Azure managed-identity access token.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are service-level domain entities used by the page code; there are no separate request/response DTO classes or immutable API records. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog-list response view model. The image uploader returns an anonymous { name, url } object serialized with JavaScriptSerializer. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL schema was found.

Communication Patterns

Page handlers call ICatalogService and IImageService synchronously in-process. The SQL-backed catalog service uses EF6 and SQL Server, while image operations can call Azure Blob Storage. There is no message broker or application gateway, and no explicit retry, circuit-breaker, or bulkhead policy was identified. Azure AD authentication is enabled conditionally; otherwise the application installs its custom OWIN authentication middleware. TLS is not forced by the container port mapping; IIS Express declares a local SSL port for development.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining an online product catalog. Catalog records include product, brand, type, pricing, and stock information; product images are managed separately.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogA product offered in the catalog, with price, inventory, and image referenceBelongs to one brand and one type
CatalogBrandCatalogBrand or manufacturer associated with catalog itemsCan be associated with many catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalogProduct category/type used for catalog classificationCan classify many catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsProduct CatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server or mock data; optional Azure Blob Storage

There are no separate business microservices or cross-context data exchange flows in this solution.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog or requests a page using the pagination route.
  2. The Web Forms page applies the default page size/index or reads route values.
  3. ICatalogService retrieves and orders catalog entries, with brand and type information.
  4. The page computes image URLs and renders the page of products.

When mock data is enabled, reads come from the in-memory catalog; otherwise the service reads through EF6 from SQL Server.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. An authenticated editor submits catalog fields from the Create or Edit page.
  2. The page checks ModelState; CatalogItem defines price and stock range constraints.
  3. The service creates or updates the item in the selected backing store.
  4. If a temporary image name was supplied, the image service promotes the image to the item’s image location.
  5. The page redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Upload and remove product images

The ASMX image method receives a multipart upload, decodes the stream, and accepts only JPEG, PNG, or GIF image formats. Valid uploads are stored as temporary images by the configured image service. The Delete page confirms and removes a catalog record through ICatalogService.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No application service aggregation or cross-service business data flow was identified. The catalog service reads and writes catalog data in the same SQL database (or its mock implementation); the image service stores image content in Azure Blob Storage when enabled. Catalog item image URLs reference the resulting image location.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Editor as "Catalog Editor" participant Page as "Create or Edit Page" participant Catalog as "Catalog Service" participant DB as "SQL Server or Mock Catalog" participant Image as "Image Service" participant Blob as "Azure Blob Storage" Editor->>Page: Submit catalog fields and optional image Page->>Page: Check ModelState and item rules alt Input invalid Page-->>Editor: Re-render page with validation errors else Input valid Page->>Catalog: CreateCatalogItem or UpdateCatalogItem Catalog->>DB: Save catalog item DB-->>Catalog: Save result opt Temporary image supplied Page->>Image: Promote temporary image Image->>Blob: Copy image to item location Blob-->>Image: Copy result Image-->>Page: Image update complete end Page-->>Editor: Redirect to catalog end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • CatalogItem requires a positive price with at most two decimal places and applies configured ranges to price and stock fields.
  • Catalog items reference one catalog brand and one catalog type; the EF model requires both relationships.
  • Product IDs are generated from HiLo SQL sequences in SQL mode and from the current maximum mock ID in mock mode.
  • Image upload accepts only decoded JPEG, PNG, or GIF content; invalid content returns HTTP 400.
  • Catalog persistence and image storage are separate operations; there is no distributed transaction or compensating workflow identified.
  • OWIN authentication can use Azure AD when configured; otherwise custom middleware is installed. Catalog maintenance pages check request authentication.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy Web Forms, Entity Framework 6, OWIN, and older Azure SDK packages. The package list contains multiple older framework-support packages and a prerelease 2.0.0-beta Configuration Builders family; compatibility should be checked when modernizing the target runtime or Azure integrations.

  • packages.config lists installed packages, including transitive dependencies; the 147 entries are not all direct references.
  • Azure Blob Storage, Azure AD, Redis session support, and Service Bus packages are present, but not all are enabled or used by the current default configuration.
  • Entity Framework 6.3.0 is the only ORM package family; no EF Core dependency is declared.
  • No test-scoped packages or test project were found in this solution.

Caching Strategy

No application-level or EF query cache was identified. The mock catalog is held in memory for the process lifetime. Redis session-state provider configuration exists only as a commented example in Web.config; no active Redis cache configuration was found.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The web application is the only application service in the solution and owns the complete catalog database; no service-to-service database sharing or CQRS boundary is present. Catalog reads and writes go through ICatalogService; the SQL implementation uses one EF context per lifetime scope, while the mock implementation mutates its local collection. Images are stored in the separate pics Azure Blob container when Azure storage is enabled.
